description: EcoOrbit is an interactive web simulation dashboard designed to evaluate shifting AI and compute different workloads from Earth to Low earth orbit (LEO).Our goal to calculate terrestrial carbon/energy savings while monitoring orbital debris collision risks using open NASA data.
summary: EcoOrbit is an innovative AI compute and LEO orbital sustainability engine developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project provides an interactive simulation framework designed to evaluate the offloading of heavy, non-latency-critical artificial intelligence and large language model training workloads from carbon-heavy, water-depleting terrestrial data centers into solar-powered satellites in Low Earth Orbit. The platform features three core technical pillars: zero-emission compute running on continuous solar energy, deep-space radiative cooling to eliminate freshwater consumption, and debris mitigation integration utilizing live NORAD catalog telemetry to assess Kessler Syndrome risk indices. By integrating open data from CelesTrak, NASA's Orbital Debris Program Office, and the U.S. Department of Energy, EcoOrbit demonstrates a scientifically grounded pathway toward sustainable hybrid computing infrastructure.
details: EcoOrbit is an interactive simulation engine that evaluates offloading heavy AI and LLM workloads from carbon-heavy terrestrial data centers into solar-powered LEO satellites. Built using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, and Plotly (alongside live CelesTrak API telemetry), it lets users adjust simulation parameters to instantly visualize CO₂ savings, water conservation, and orbital risks. The project tackles power grid congestion and freshwater depletion by harnessing continuous space solar power and deep-space radiative cooling. It creatively bridges climate sustainability with orbital safety, carefully balancing Earth conservation against Kessler Syndrome risks using NASA Orbital Debris and U.S. Department of Energy data.
